title: Certificate III in Animal Care Services
rules_text:
To achieve this qualification, competency must be demonstrated in:
17 units of competency:
7 core units plus
10 elective units.
Elective units must ensure the integrity of the qualification’s Australian Qualifications Framework (AQF) alignment and contribute to a valid, industry-supported vocational outcome. Electives can be chosen to provide a general qualification or a qualification with a specialisation.
For the award of the Certificate III in Animal Care Services choose:
at least 9 units from the electives in Groups A to D
up to 1 unit from any currently endorsed Training Package or accredited course.
For the award of the Certificate III in Animal Care Services (Animal Care) choose:
at least 4 units from the electives in Group A
up to 6 units from the electives listed in Groups A to D (not already selected)
up to 1 unit from any currently endorsed Training Package or accredited course.
For the award of the Certificate III in Animal Care Services (Pet Grooming) choose:
all 6 units from the electives in Group B
up to 4 units from the electives listed in Groups A to D (not already selected)
up to 1 unit from any currently endorsed Training Package or accredited course.
For the award of the Certificate III in Animal Care Services (Customer Service) choose:
the following units from Group C:
ACMGEN205 Source and provide information for animal care needs
ACMGEN305 Provide advice on companion animal selection and general care
BSBOPS304 Deliver and monitor a service to customers
at least 1 more unit from the electives in Group C
up to 6 units from the electives listed in Groups A to D (not already selected)
up to 1 unit from any currently endorsed Training Package or accredited course.
Where two specialisations are completed, award of the qualification would read (for example), Certificate III in Animal Care Services (Pet Grooming, Customer Service).

title: Certificate IV in Equine Care
rules_text:
To achieve this qualification, competency must be demonstrated in:
15 units of competency:
7 core units plus
8 elective units.
The electives are to be chosen as follows:
at least 1 and up to 2 units from Group A
up to 7 units from Groups B to F
up to 2 units from this or any other endorsed training package or accredited course.
Elective units must ensure the integrity of the qualification’s Australian Qualifications Framework (AQF) alignment and contribute to a valid, industry-supported vocational outcome.
Any combination of electives that meets the packaging rules above can be selected for the award of the ACM40921 Certificate IV in Equine Care.
Where appropriate, electives may be packaged to provide a qualification with a specialisation area as follows:
at least 3 units from Group B electives for the award of the Certificate IV in Equine Care (Fitness and Performance Training)
at least 3 units from Group C electives for the award of the Certificate IV in Equine Care (Horse Educator)
at least 2 units from Group D electives for the award of the Certificate IV in Equine Care (Gear Fitter and Checker)
1 elective unit from Group E in for the award of the Certificate IV in Equine Care (Horse Clipper).
Where two specialisations are completed, award of the qualification would read (for example), Certificate IV in Equine Care(Fitness and Performance Training and Horse Education).
